tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md, the workspace map: it introduces the astrophysics research portfolio (black holes, wormholes, exotic compact objects, exoplanets), the installed scientific stack, and where each project lives. CONTEXT.md complements it with the operating conventions agents and loops follow, so read both before touching anything else.

tour.title: Theory and Symbolic Models
tour.description: The physics starts in writing: premium/theory_black_holes.md and the other premium documents collect the derivations, while THEORY.md indexes the theory program. models/equations.py is the most-depended-on code file in the graph — it turns those derivations into symbolic Kerr/orbital expressions every notebook and check reuses.
tour.languageLesson: Python's sympy lets derivations stay symbolic: equations.py defines exact Kerr expressions (Christoffel symbols, ISCO radii) that later scripts evaluate numerically only at the edges, keeping round-off out of the physics.

tour.title: Research Wiki
tour.description: research/wiki/index.md links the Obsidian-style wiki articles that grow alongside the premium theory documents — catalog surveys, accretion, perturbation theory. The wiki is deliberately cross-linked so new theory work can check which claims already exist before adding new ones.

tour.title: Computational Notebooks
tour.description: The notebooks package turns theory into results: 01_exotic_compact_objects_fundamentals.ipynb lays the foundations, and the newest member 25_gw_real_analysis.ipynb runs a real GWOSC strain analysis with PyCBC, Bilby and EinsteinPy. Each notebook is generated and re-executed by the workspace's notebook-health loop, so they stay runnable rather than rotting.

tour.title: Data Pipelines
tour.description: Catalogs enter the workspace through focused downloaders: scripts/download_gwosc.py pulls the GWTC event API, scripts/download_heasarc.py queries HEASARC TAP, and scripts/process_blackcat.py cleans the BlackCAT dynamical black-hole sample. Together they feed every dashboard and report downstream.

tour.title: Catalog Snapshot and Refresh Reports
tour.description: The pipelines land in SQLite: research/projects/black-holes/data/black_holes.sqlite stores the GWTC snapshot (gwtc_events) plus a fetch_log of every refresh. reports/latest.md — regenerated on each data refresh — explains in plain language what the 391-event snapshot means, its units and caveats, while reports/summary.md aggregates project-level results.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite databases are single-file, zero-admin stores — ideal for reproducible research snapshots. Keeping a fetch_log table next to the science table makes every snapshot auditable: you can always answer 'which pull produced these rows?'

tour.title: Verification
tour.description: Claims are checked, not assumed: scripts/verify_formulas.py re-derives the symbolic results, and research/projects/black-holes-wormholes/scripts/kerr_isco_exact.py validates the exact Kerr ISCO radius against the notebook implementation with an explicit error budget. These checks gate the notebooks and figures the workspace publishes.

tour.title: Graphs and Automation
tour.description: The workspace runs itself: .opencode/loops/refresh-data.sh orchestrates the download-process-report sweep you saw in steps 5-6, docs/GRAPHS.md documents the three Understand-Anything knowledge graphs, and .ua/tools/add-cohesion-edges.py stitches evidence-backed cross-links into the code graph after every refresh. This tour itself lives inside that graph.
